story.iWant: to identify clear periods between rain windows
story.soThat: users can find safe timeframes for outdoor activities
story.tasks:
- Task 1: Extend rain-windows module with safe window calculation (AC: 1, 2, 3) - Add `SafeWindow` interface to `/will-it-rain/lib/rain-windows.ts` matching `RainWindow` structure - Implement `calculateSafeWindows()` function accepting `RainWindow[]` array as input - Calculate gaps between consecutive rain windows (end of window N → start of window N+1) - Filter out safe windows with duration < 1 hour (< 60 minutes) - Return array of safe windows in chronological order - Export function for use by Story 2.6 API integration
- Task 2: Handle clear period after last rain window (AC: 5) - Accept forecast end time as parameter (e.g., current time + 24 hours) - Calculate safe window from end of last rain window to forecast end time - Apply same 1-hour minimum duration filter - Include "after rain" safe window in results if duration ≥ 1 hour - Handle case where last rain window ends very close to forecast end (< 1 hour remaining)
- Task 3: Handle edge cases and single rain window scenarios (AC: 4, 7) - Handle empty rain windows array (no rain detected) → return empty safe windows array - Handle single rain window (only one rain period) → calculate only "after rain" safe window if applicable - Handle multiple rain windows with some gaps < 1 hour → filter out short gaps - Handle rain windows that span most of 24 hours → minimal or no safe windows - Ensure no off-by-one errors in time calculations
- Task 4: Reuse time formatting from Story 2.4 (AC: 6) - Import `formatTimeRange()` from rain-windows.ts (already exists from Story 2.4) - Use same 12-hour AM/PM formatting for safe window display - Ensure consistent time formatting between rain windows and safe windows - No additional time formatting logic needed (already implemented)
- Task 5: Return structured safe windows for API consumption (AC: 1, 2) - Return `SafeWindow[]` array with start/end Date objects - Ensure TypeScript strict mode compliance (no `any` types) - Prepare for integration with Story 2.6 (API response formatting) - Structure output to match SafeWindow interface from tech spec
- Task 6: Manual testing and verification (AC: 1-7) - Test with multiple rain windows and gaps between them (e.g., morning rain, afternoon rain) - Test with single rain window ending mid-day (verify "after rain" safe window detected) - Test with gaps < 1 hour duration (verify filtering works) - Test with gaps ≥ 1 hour duration (verify included in results) - Test with no rain windows (empty array) → expect empty safe windows - Test with rain windows spanning most of 24 hours → expect minimal safe windows - Test edge case: last rain window ends < 1 hour before forecast end - Verify time formatting displays correctly in 12-hour AM/PM format - TypeScript compilation passes (`npm run type-check`) - ESLint validation passes (`npm run lint`)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
1. **Given** detected rain windows within 24 hours **When** I calculate safe windows **Then** gaps between rain periods are identified as safe windows **And** each safe window has accurate start time (end of previous rain period) and end time (start of next rain period) **And** safe windows are returned in chronological order
2. **Given** multiple rain windows exist with gaps between them **When** I calculate safe windows **Then** each gap between consecutive rain windows is identified as a separate safe window **And** the start time of each safe window equals the end time of the previous rain window **And** the end time of each safe window equals the start time of the next rain window
3. **Given** a safe window has a very short duration **When** I filter safe windows **Then** safe windows shorter than 1 hour (< 60 minutes) are excluded from the results **And** only safe windows ≥ 1 hour duration are included in the output **And** minimum duration filtering ensures users only see meaningful safe periods
4. **Given** there is only one rain window in the 24-hour period **When** I calculate safe windows **Then** no safe windows between rain periods are returned (empty array for gaps) **And** the clear period after the last rain window until end of forecast is identified (if ≥ 1 hour) **And** single rain period scenarios are handled correctly
5. **Given** rain windows end before the 24-hour forecast ends **When** I calculate safe windows **Then** the clear period after the last rain window is identified as a safe window **And** the safe window starts at the end time of the last rain period **And** the safe window ends at the end of the 24-hour forecast period **And** this "after rain" safe window is included only if duration ≥ 1 hour
6. **Given** safe window times need to be user-friendly **When** I format time strings **Then** times use 12-hour format with AM/PM (e.g., "5:00 PM - 9:00 PM") **And** time formatting uses native Intl.DateTimeFormat (reuses existing formatTimeRange from Story 2.4) **And** safe window times are displayed in a readable, consistent format
7. **Given** there are no rain windows detected (no rain in 24 hours) **When** I calculate safe windows **Then** no safe windows are returned (empty array) **And** the entire 24-hour period is clear (handled implicitly by NO answer) **And** edge case of zero rain windows does not cause errors

doc.title: Epic 2 Technical Specification - Weather Intelligence Engine
doc.snippet: Enhances /lib/rain-windows.ts with safe window logic. Implements clear period detection between rain events. Calculates gaps between consecutive rain windows (end of window N → start of window N+1). Applies 1-hour minimum duration filter. Handles "after rain" safe window (clear period after last rain until forecast end).

doc.title: Architecture Document
doc.snippet: No database, no caching, fresh data every request. Pure functions with no side effects. Weather data must be fresh. All calculations are stateless and deterministic.

doc.title: Architecture Document
doc.snippet: Use native Date and Intl.DateTimeFormat (no Day.js or date-fns). Zero bundle size. Intl.DateTimeFormat handles 12-hour AM/PM formatting. Sufficient for simple formatting needs.

constraint.rule: Stateless pure functions only - no side effects, no external dependencies, no API calls, no database queries (ADR-002)
Extend existing will-it-rain/lib/rain-windows.ts module. Add SafeWindow interface and calculateSafeWindows() function to same file as RainWindow and detectRainWindows()
TypeScript strict mode required. No 'any' types permitted. Input: RainWindow[] from Story 2.4. Output: SafeWindow[] with identical structure (start/end Date properties)
Reuse existing formatTimeRange() function from rain-windows.ts. DO NOT recreate time formatting logic. Use native Intl.DateTimeFormat (no date libraries)
Safe windows must be ≥ 1 hour (60 minutes) duration. Filter out gaps shorter than 60 minutes. Rationale: Very short gaps aren't meaningful for planning outdoor activities
Calculate safe window from end of last rain window to forecast end time (current time + 24 hours). Include only if duration ≥ 1 hour. Requires forecastEndTime parameter
Manual testing only (no automated unit tests until Epic 5). Create comprehensive manual test suite with hardcoded test data. TypeScript type-check and ESLint validation required
Comprehensive JSDoc comments required (follow Story 2.4 pattern). Explain algorithm, edge cases, parameters, and return values

interface.name: SafeWindow
interface.signature: interface SafeWindow { start: Date; end: Date; }
interface.description: Identical structure to RainWindow interface. Represents a clear period between rain windows where users can safely plan outdoor activities

interface.name: calculateSafeWindows
interface.signature: function calculateSafeWindows(rainWindows: RainWindow[], forecastEndTime: Date): SafeWindow[]
interface.description: Pure function accepting rain windows array and forecast end time. Returns array of safe windows (gaps between rain periods ≥ 1 hour). Applies minimum duration filter. Handles "after rain" safe window calculation

interface.name: formatTimeRange (reuse)
interface.signature: function formatTimeRange(start: Date, end: Date): string
interface.description: Already exists from Story 2.4. Returns 12-hour AM/PM formatted time range (e.g., "5:00 PM - 9:00 PM"). DO NOT recreate - import and reuse

interface.name: RainWindow (from Story 2.4)
interface.signature: interface RainWindow { start: Date; end: Date; }
interface.description: Input type for calculateSafeWindows(). Represents continuous rain period detected by detectRainWindows() function

test.scenario: Multiple rain windows with gaps ≥ 1 hour

ideas.test: Verify safe windows detected correctly. Create test data with 2+ rain windows separated by 1-2 hour gaps. Expect safe window array with correct start/end times matching gaps.
Verify start time of safe window = end time of previous rain window. Verify end time of safe window = start time of next rain window. Test chronological ordering.

test.scenario: Gaps shorter than 1 hour filtered out

ideas.test: Create rain windows with 30-minute and 45-minute gaps. Expect these gaps filtered out (not in results). Only gaps ≥ 60 minutes included.
Test with only one rain window ending mid-day. Expect no gap safe windows (empty array for gaps). Verify "after rain" safe window detected if applicable.
Rain window ends at hour 18, forecast ends at hour 24 (6 hours remaining). Expect safe window from hour 18 to hour 24. Test with < 1 hour remaining (should not create safe window).
Verify safe window times formatted in 12-hour AM/PM format. Compare with formatTimeRange() output to ensure consistency with rain windows.
Pass empty RainWindow[] array. Expect empty SafeWindow[] array returned. Verify no errors thrown.

test.scenario: Rain windows spanning most of 24 hours

ideas.test: Test with rain windows covering hours 0-20 with minimal gaps. Expect minimal or no safe windows. Verify filtering logic works correctly.
Create rain windows with exactly 60-minute gap. Expect safe window included (≥ 1 hour condition is inclusive).
Create rain windows with 59-minute gap. Expect gap filtered out (< 1 hour). Verify boundary condition.
